conflicts.text: rehearsal: the cheapest model reads a ticket cold three times and tries to build it on paper, so "buildable as written" is measured. → CodeMother
conflicts.ticket_says: The rehearsal is handed the plan steps plus a WHAT EXISTS section built before the read by extracting and measuring what exists (paths, modules). The prompt says 'you are a build simulator here to identify what's missing' and judges build steps only, never the process.
conflicts.why: Outline 17.6 states rehearsal 'reads a ticket cold three times' — meaning reading without prior knowledge of what exists. The ticket's why section quotes Akien: 'we should be telling it what exists and what doesn't before hand,' directly contradicting reading cold. The measured facts about existence must be given upfront, or it's not reading cold. Additionally, outline says 'tries to build it on paper' (simulating a full build process) but ticket says 'judges build steps only, never the process' — if you don't understand the process, you cannot meaningfully simulate a build.
